subject: Escalation: Acme private offer — revised rev-share + net45 invoicing request
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme private offer — initial ask

Karthik,

Quick context: Acme Energies (Julia Park) has committed to a 24-month seats-and-usage subscription for our hosted inference product but routed the purchase through AWS Private Offers. They want two non-standard items that require Deal Desk / exec signoff:

1) Rev-share carve: they are asking for a blended Marketplace rev-share of 70/30 (Redwood/AWS) for first 12 months, then revert to our standard 85/15 for the remainder. This would reduce our take in year 1; finance flagged it as material.

2) Net45 invoicing + onboarding credit: Acme insists on net45 (we default to net30 for Marketplace invoiced customers) and a $40k one-time onboarding credit applied against first invoice.

Attached is the proposed MA (Acme_MA_v2.pdf) and my revshare projection (revshare_model_acme.xlsx). We need an executive approval or clear denial so I can finalize the Private Offer request with AWS.

Ask: Can you evaluate whether we can approve a 70/30 split for 12 months + net45 + $40k credit? If not, what is the minimum concession we can offer that keeps ARR economics acceptable?

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Strategic GTM — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme private offer — initial ask

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the files. I ran a preliminary margin sensitivity against the deal economics: at a 70/30 split in year 1, our gross contribution in year 1 drops ~18% vs standard terms, primarily because the customer will be net-new and front-loaded. The $40k onboarding credit worsens the upfront payback, but the 24-month term gives some recovery in year 2.

A few operational notes for the Private Offer flow with AWS:
- Marketplace listings require that we register the final rev-share percentage in the private offer metadata. AWS will enforce it for the duration of the offer window.
- Net45 is doable but will push the billing to Marketplace ops and may delay cash recognition by ~15 days compared to net30. Finance signaled we need an exec waiver for >net30 on Marketplace deals.

Proposed compromise to present to Acme and Ops:
- Offer 72/28 for months 0–12 (slightly better for us than 70/30) with a performance stub: if ACV usage in months 1–6 exceeds forecast by >15%, we roll to 78/22 for months 7–12.
- Reduce onboarding credit to $25k and apply it as a one-time usage credit in month 1.
- Approve net45 only if Acme signs a purchase order that references the Private Offer ID and commits to the 24-month term.

If Execs approve that structure, we can push the Private Offer to AWS marketplace-ops and include the conditional performance bump. Otherwise, the alternative is stick to our standard 85/15 and offer a $15k credit.

Next step from my side: I can draft exact language for the private offer metadata and a companion SOW bullet. Do you want me to spin that up and loop in Marketplace Ops?

- Karthik
Senior Deal Desk Manager
From: Julia Park <julia.park@acme-energies.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: marketplace-ops@amazon.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:47:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Acme private offer — initial ask

Karthik / Marissa,

Appreciate the rapid review. A few clarifications from Acme: the onboarding credit is important to offset our professional services ramp (we've budgeted for ~6 weeks of integration). Net45 is non-negotiable for our procurement schedule.

We are open to a performance-linked revision in month 6/7 as long as the initial guarantee is documented in the Private Offer metadata and the billing cadence is clear. If Redwood is willing to adjust to ~72/28 in year 1 with the conditional bump, we can sign the PO this week. Please include Marketplace Ops in the final offer so we know how the credit will be applied.

Julia
VP, Cloud Partnerships — Acme Energies

--- Forwarded message attached to this thread for record: purchase_intent_acme.pdf (referenced in Acme PO)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: Exec signoff request — Acme private offer (72/28 yr1, net45, $25k credit)

Jonas / Vanessa —

Need quick exec approval to finalize this Private Offer with Acme. Summary of proposed exception: 72/28 rev-share for months 0–12 with a conditional bump to 78/22 if usage > forecast by 15% in months 1–6; Net45 invoicing; one-time $25k onboarding credit applied as usage credit. Deal: 24-month committed term, expected ARR on Redwood books $1.2M year 1 (post rev-share).

Why this is recommended:
- Strategic customer in energy sector; potential to be a reference in our utility vertical (strong GTM motion).
- Acme routes via AWS Marketplace which gives us faster procurement and sticky renewal cadence.
- If we decline, Acme will likely delay purchase or push to another vendor.

Risks:
- Short-term unit economics degrade in year 1. Finance has flagged margin impact of ~18% vs standard on-year contribution.
- Operational: needs Marketplace Ops coordination to bake the credit into the private offer metadata.

Files attached for review: Acme_MA_v2.pdf, revshare_model_acme.xlsx.

Decision options (please reply-all):
A) Approve as proposed (72/28 yr1, conditional bump, net45, $25k credit) — we will proceed to register private offer with AWS.
B) Approve with tighter credit or net30 only — we will counteroffer to Acme.
C) Decline — revert to standard 85/15 + $15k credit.

Can you indicate decision by end of day tomorrow so I can lock private-offer metadata with marketplace-ops?

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Strategic GTM — Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Exec signoff request — Acme private offer (72/28 yr1, net45, $25k credit)

Marissa / team —

I approve option A with a single commercial caveat: add a 6-month early-termination recoup clause. If Acme terminates before month 12, we recover the onboarding credit pro-rata and revert to standard revenue recognition for any unsettled Marketplace adjustments. Karthik — please draft the clause.

Also, finance should confirm a one-off accounting treatment for the onboarding credit to ensure revenue catch-up in year 2. Vanessa — loop in Rev Ops to make sure the Private Offer metadata, PO language, and our internal billing route are aligned before marketplace submission.

Jonas Weber
VP, GTM Operations — Redwood Inference
